A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RelightAnyone paper and complete supplementary material. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research content, equations, figures, tables, and supplement are unchanged; differences concern the version stamp and bibliography.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and relighting experiments, quantitative results in Tables 1–2, and supplementary ablations and failure cases in Section 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and the qualitative evaluations, ablations, and failure cases throughout the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-stage Gaussian avatar model, dataset-specific lighting code, relighting network, losses, and inversion/finetuning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use 3DPR, Ava-256, SDFM, and Nersemble, alongside the same in-the-wild images. Single-image and multi-view reconstruction, relighting, and novel-view scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain NeRFFaceLighting, Lite2Relight, and 3DPR in Table 2 and Figure 10, and IC-Light and DiffusionRenderer in Figure 9. The single-stage ablation comparator is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The datasets' splits, preprocessing, training settings, and evaluation procedures are identical. These include the 116/11 training/test split for D1, 10×20 environment maps for Table 2, and PSNR, RMSE, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and supplementary Section 7 retain identical analyses of the two-stage design, lighting codes, finetuning, regularization, OLAT/full-on data coverage, and accessory and hairstyle failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains the two-stage PSNR of 30.06, and Table 2 retains single-image and multi-view PSNR values of 26.57 and 29.07.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(17), including reflectance parameterization and training objectives, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about generalized relightable avatars, learning from mixed flat-lit and OLAT datasets, and fitting unseen subjects.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including explanations of lighting alignment and regularization, neutral-expression restrictions, and failures involving hair, glasses, and headscarves.

D1.justification: Data-processing instructions and supplementary Section 6 are unchanged, including architecture details, loss weights, learning rates, batch size, GPU hardware, training duration, and fitting time. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference [60] remains the same 3DPR work; v2 adds its ACM SIGGRAPH ASIA 2025 Conference Proceedings venue, which is a bibliographic metadata update.

P1.justification: v2 updates the arXiv version/date stamp and supplies publication-venue metadata for reference [60]. The main text, supplementary prose, terminology, and section organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The expanded reference [60] causes limited bibliography reflow on PDF pages 11–12, including moving the end of reference [69] onto page 12. Figures 1–17, Tables 1–2, and the research and supplementary layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 completes the venue information for reference [60], with minor bibliography reflow and an updated version stamp. The scientific content, empirical support, reproducibility details, and limitations are identical, so these editorial changes do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
